summary: Added LivingProcessGroups (a ProcessTable double whose signal(pid,0) succeeds only when pid is in its alive set and throws ESRCH otherwise), InProcessRun.checkedDelivery (builds the real CheckedRunDelivery with a ToolRunner over a scripted git, gh and node refusing with UnscriptedRequest, and signal wired to the double) and InProcessRun.intended (writes intent.json with the same machineDigest formula #requireIntentIdentity checks). checked-run-delivery-process-groups.test.ts proves R4 (this-repository.md:119-141): a publication whose push process group is alive reads as publishing with diagnostic 'push process group 4242 is still running', both when the group's leader pid is also alive and when only the negative group id is alive (leader dead) — the second case is the one that would go 'uncertain' instead of 'publishing' if the ownership check ever used the wrong sign, which I confirmed by mutating LivingProcessGroups.signal to always refuse and watching both cases fail for that reason before reverting. The git capture captures/git/ls-remote-absent-branch.txt was taken from a real `git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/feat/7` against a scratch bare origin with no such branch (exit 0, empty stdout/stderr), run under the session scratchpad. All four verification commands of the task pass, as do the other in-process suites that consume the modified in-process-run.ts fixture (restart-recovery, run-driver-runtime, run-driver, run-recovery).

summary: Added the two deliver() retry cases exactly as named in the brief's TDD/Tests lines, in a new describe block reusing LivePushScenario.arranged(). deliver() (unlike inspect(), which is all task 3's tests exercised) also runs #requireWorkspaceIdentity and #requirePinned before the push retry, so five more real git captures were needed beyond the plan's explicit push-rejected.txt (symbolic-ref, rev-parse, status, worktree-list, remote-get-url) plus the reused ls-remote-absent-branch.txt; all were produced from one real scratch git repository built under the scratchpad (never pushed to a real remote, a local bare repo with a rejecting pre-receive hook stood in for the retry push's origin). LivePushScenario.SHA changed from the placeholder 'c'.repeat(40) to the real captured commit sha (da0a450ab847474c2645862ad63d9231ee93d47c) so rev-parse HEAD's capture matches intent.sha; this is harmless for task 3's two existing tests since inspect() never reaches those git calls. The worktree-list capture embeds a <worktree> placeholder for the absolute path (a fresh mkdtemp checkout each run can't be known ahead of time) substituted with run.checkout at arrange time; #gitText trims the result so the extra format slack is inert. LivePushScenario.#ATTEMPT became a public ATTEMPT so both new tests can address the pre-arranged push attempt's disposition.json by its one true name instead of duplicating the literal. arranged() now also returns the ScriptedConversation double itself so assertions land on the port's observable requests (no second push in case 1, exactly one in case 2) rather than only on journal side effects. gh and node stay fully refused in both new tests: deliver() throws inside the push retry before ever reaching them, and case 2's closing inspect() call hits the refused gh port, which CheckedRunDelivery.inspect() already catches internally and reports as kind:'uncertain' -- satisfying 'not delivered' with no gh capture needed. Since this task adds no production code (per its own 'No code' line), TDD was honored by temporarily perturbing the alive sets of both new cases and confirming each named assertion (the RunDeliveryUncertain message in case 1, the RunDeliveryFailure/disposition outcome in case 2) fails for the stated reason before restoring the real arrange. All three verification commands pass: npm run typecheck, vitest run on checked-run-delivery-process-groups.test.ts + process-ratchet.test.ts (10 tests, all green, no spawned process), and the push-rejected.txt header check.
